title: Federal Plan Requirements for Other Solid Waste Incineration Units That Commenced Construction on or before August 31, 2020, and Have Not Been Modified or Reconstructed after August 29, 2025
pass_4_primary_concern: The main concern is whether the covered-universe estimate and no-additional-cost claim are sufficiently grounded in the state-plan assumptions and supporting memoranda.
pass_5_high_stakes_domain_reason: The rule governs hazardous air emissions, compliance obligations, and public implementation burdens.
pass_5_concise_why: The proposal is structurally coherent and supported by memoranda, but the future state-plan assumptions and the compressed burden discussion still deserve comment-level scrutiny.
pass_5_most_important_consequence: If the inventory assumptions change, the final covered universe and implementation burden could shift before the record fully explains why.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The rule uses the expected federal-plan authority rather than substituting the wrong legal actor or legal source.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: If commenters want a legal argument, they should focus on statutory fit rather than role confusion.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal does not appear to invert an exception into the main source of authority.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Commenters should focus on the clarity of the statutory trigger, not on a reverse-grant theory.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The rule does not materially shift accountability away from the authority that will administer the plan.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: This is not a strong accountability-inversion record.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal relies on state-plan submissions and negative declarations as part of the implementation trigger, which is normal for a federal-plan structure but still worth tracking carefully.

evidence.quote_or_absence: The federal plan depends on whether States or Tribes submit approvable plans and whether the inventory assumptions hold.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask EPA to spell out how it will verify state-plan status and what happens if a submission is late or incomplete.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The record does not show a sequencing defect that would force the wrong burden to happen first.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: No substantial sequencing problem is visible in the available record.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal says it adds no new controls or costs, but that statement still depends on assumptions about the covered universe and on prior-rule cost treatment.

evidence.quote_or_absence: The proposed Federal plan, which adopts the model rule standards and associated requirements in the revised EGs, would not result in any additional control requirements or impose any additional costs above those previously considered in the 2025 revised OSWI EG.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask EPA to show why the record is enough to support the no-additional-cost conclusion under different state-plan outcomes.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The federal-plan remedy fits the stated rationale of implementing the revised emission guidelines when state or tribal plans are absent.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: The remedy looks aligned with the stated objective.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The implementation story is credible but compressed; the notice does not fully show how different authorities will absorb the transition work if plan status changes.

evidence.quote_or_absence: The average annual Agency burden and cost during the three years of the ICR is estimated to be 1,335 hours at a cost of $75,700.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask for a by-authority implementation map showing what each state, tribal, and delegated agency must do.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal does not depend on a single opaque technical interface in a way that looks magical or unsupported.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: No obvious magic-interface problem appears in the current record.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The harmful condition the rule addresses is clear: implementation of the revised OSWI emission guidelines where state or tribal plans are not effective.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Threat definition is not the main issue here.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The summary downplays incremental burdens by framing the proposal as having no additional control requirements and only de minimis burden change, even though the rule still creates planning and reporting work.

evidence.quote_or_absence: The proposed Federal plan would not result in any additional control requirements or impose any additional costs above those previously considered in the 2025 revised OSWI EG.
The average annual burden to industry over the next three years from these recordkeeping and reporting requirements is estimated to be 2,722 hours.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask EPA to distinguish average burden from transition burden and explain who bears the work of making the plan operational.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal does not create a visible viewpoint- or geography-targeting surface in the available record.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: No targetability problem is apparent from the record.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The rule includes public-comment, hearing, docket, and recordkeeping mechanisms that function as ordinary safeguards.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: The safeguards picture is not a serious defect on this record.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal does push substantial recordkeeping and reporting work onto regulated units, but that burden is disclosed in the ICR materials and looks ordinary for this kind of plan.

evidence.quote_or_absence: The average annual burden to industry over the next three years from these recordkeeping and reporting requirements is estimated to be 2,722 hours.
The total operation and maintenance (O&M) costs for this ICR are $87,000.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Commenters can ask whether the burden estimates reflect transition work and not just steady-state reporting.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The plan does not turn ordinary conduct into suspicion-based treatment in the available record.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: No suspicion-machine defect is visible here.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal uses reporting and ICIS/ECHO-style data flows rather than degrading the audit trail.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: The recordkeeping structure looks like a normal accountability substrate, not a weakened one.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal keeps the ordinary comment and implementation sequence intact, so harm-before-review is not the main issue on this record.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: No obvious harm-before-review problem is visible.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The state-plan trigger is a gate, but it is a conventional and disclosed federal-plan gate rather than an opaque chokepoint.

evidence.quote_or_absence: If a State or Tribe with existing OSWI units subject to the 2025 revised OSWI emission guidelines does not submit an approvable plan by June 30, 2027, the EPA will develop, implement, and enforce a Federal plan for existing OSWI units located in that State or area of Indian Country.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask EPA to clarify the state-by-state transition path if a plan is late or rejected.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The rule separates routine reporting burden, state-plan timing, and emission-control consequences well enough for comment purposes.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Consequence-class ambiguity is not a major defect here.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The proposal does not use vague standards as the main exclusion mechanism.
pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: No meaningful ambiguity-enabled gatekeeping appears in the available record.

pass_5_flaws.explanation: The record is mostly coherent: authority, inventory, emissions, and burden materials fit together, but the future state-plan assumptions still create some pressure.

evidence.quote_or_absence: Presuming that State plans that have already been submitted to EPA will be approved, that any State indicating its intent to submit a plan will follow through with an approvable State plan, and that any negative declaration submitted by a State is accurate, we estimate that 59 OSWI units in 11 States will be covered by the Federal plan.
The average annual Agency burden and cost during the three years of the ICR is estimated to be 1,335 hours at a cost of $75,700.

pass_5_flaws.comment_leverage: Ask EPA to add a short sensitivity table and a clearer implementation crosswalk.
